title: Staggered roadmap sync scratch - product/eng/ml
content:
Meeting: cross-functional roadmap alignment (staggered rollout)
Date / Time: 2026-08-05 10:00–11:00 PT (prep notes: Sofia)
Attendees to ping: Kai (Product), Ravi (Serving Runtime), Leah (Applied ML), Marcus (Infra), optional: Leah's quant team lead (TBD)

Primary goal (1): Agree phase gates and metric thresholds for the Q4 model rollout for low-latency chat model variant (sparse-8q + KV cache + prefetched prompts)
Secondary goal (2): Surface capacity and SLO tradeoffs so product can pick a default routing policy (latency-first vs cost-first)
Success criteria: clear Phase 0/1/2 definition, ownership for capacity checks, one deliverable action list with owners + dates

Quick context (one paragraph):
- Product wants to ship an improved chat model with context-aware recall (prefix KV caching + retrieval hints) in Q4. Applied ML has a validated 8-bit sparse quant profile that reduces GPU memory by ~35% but increases p95 latency by ~8% when batch sizes are low. Serving runtime has new continuous batching + prefetch hooks that can mask that latency if we can achieve average batch size 4+, but that requires controlling request routing and introducing a short warm-window (50–80ms). Infra capacity is tight for holiday spikes; Dedicated pools can be reserved but cost delta is material.

Agenda (40m total):
- 5m: Quick alignment on desired user experience (Kai)
- 10m: Runtime constraints and warm-window tradeoffs (Ravi)
- 10m: ML quality vs latency summary + canary dataset results (Leah)
- 10m: Deployment plan outline + infra commit ask (Marcus)
- 5m: Decision & next steps (all)

Key numbers to surface in meeting (bring these):
- Current p50/p95 for hosted baseline (gpt-like baseline): p50=45ms, p95=210ms (token generation op)
- Applied ML sparse-8q: p50=55ms, p95=225ms when batch=1; with batch>=4 p95 -> ~190ms
- Cost delta (hosted per-token): sparse-8q runtime: -18% cost/token vs baseline; Dedicated with reserved capacity can add fixed monthly cost but reduce unit cost by ~25% at scale
- Target SLO for product: p95 <= 250ms for small interactive flows; stricter SLO for high-tier customers (p95 <= 180ms)
- Estimated additional GPU hours if we cruise with warm-window prefetch: 18–24% more throughput efficiency; need to validate with synthetic trace

Hypotheses we should test before Phase 1 can be greenlit (short bullets):
- H1: Prefetch warm-window of 60ms will increase average batch size to >=3 under our traffic mix (internal webapp + mobile) — verify with production trace replay
- H2: Sparse-8q quality delta on edge cases is <1.5% A/B regression on our eval set (long-tail prompts)
- H3: Fallback to dense-16 on p95 breaches reduces incident rate by >60% without user-visible errors (needs routing test)

Proposed phase gating (staggered):
- Phase 0 (lab/canary): internal-only, run against replayed traffic, no customer traffic. Metrics: batch size >=2 avg, p95 <= 230ms, convo-quality delta <2%.
- Phase 1 (shadow + low-traffic canary): 5% of live traffic routed to new stack in shadow mode for 1 week, then 1% live traffic canary for 48 hours. Metrics: error rate <= 0.1%, p95 <= 240ms, cost delta within expected range.
- Phase 2 (region-limited rollout): enable in non-primary region (EU/APAC) for 2 weeks, monitor SLO; if stable, broaden to full rollout with automatic fallback policies.

Open questions / risks to raise in sync (short list):
- Risk: holiday traffic spike planning — infra may not be able to sustain warm-window-induced peak without extra reserved capacity. Need commitment on minimum reserved GPU pool by 2026-10-01.
- Question: What telemetry hooks do we need to alert on 'batch starvation' (when average batch drops <1.7) and automatically switch to dense-16? Who owns that automation?
- Risk: A/B eval coverage on long-tail prompts is insufficient — Leah to propose an expanded eval set (5k prompts) and sample stratification.
- Question: SLA impacts for enterprise customers when fallback triggers — need legal/CS input re: messaging and outage classification.

Prep notes / things I'll call out (Sofia):
- Bring a small visual: timeline slide showing Phase 0->2 with dates and gating metrics (one slide)
- Ask product to pick a default routing policy choice if both cost/latency acceptable (we'll need a default for API docs)
- Ask infra to quantify monthly cost delta for two reserve sizes: modest (2x current baseline) and aggressive (4x)

Immediate follow-ups I want to land in meeting and assign (actionable list):
- A1: Ravi to share synthetic trace replay results and confirm whether warm-window of 60ms is implementable without kernel changes. Due: 2026-08-12
- A2: Leah to run expanded eval (5k long-tail prompts) comparing baseline vs sparse-8q and provide a short report with failure modes. Due: 2026-08-19
- A3: Marcus to prepare infra cost delta sheet (monthly reserved vs burst) and propose minimal reserve commit by 2026-09-01. Due: 2026-08-14
- A4: Kai (Product) to decide routing default (latency-first | cost-first | hybrid) and draft a short decision note for docs. Due: 2026-08-11
- A5: Sofia to draft canary playbook skeleton (inc. rollback steps, monitoring signals), share as PR to the rollout repo. Due: 2026-08-09
- A6: All — agree on experiment cancellation thresholds (e.g., p95 > 270ms for >10% of requests for 30m) in meeting and record them. Due: meeting

Notes to self / scratches (unstructured):
- Might be worth proposing an optional 'burst cache' in infra: small LRU cache at edge to reduce cold-start on conversational prefixes.
- If we run canary on EU first, US customers might perceive regression during expansion; coordinate comms with CS sooner rather than later.
- Consider a short 'quality smoke test' that runs through 100 critical prompts post-deploy and auto-shelves rollout on failures.

Slack threads / PRs to reference during meeting: (copy/paste links)
- #engine-rolling (Slack) — thread about warm-window prototype
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-rollout-proposal/pull/78 (has rollout diagram)
- Jira: RDW-2210 (canary infra tickets)

Decision log (to fill in during meeting):
- Chosen routing policy: 
- Phase 0 go/no-go: 
- Reserved infra commit: 

End of prep notes. Keep this doc as the canonical scratchpad for the sync. After meeting I'll convert action items to individual tickets and update the rollout PR with the phase gates and thresholds. Note-to-self: capture the meeting minutes in Confluence and link back here.
